gen-gf-revalia-fs-bespoke-slab: Revalia strides across the line with widely separated letters and a lowercase g whose lower curve stays open, loud and loose. Bespoke Slab, a tall-bodied serif, keeps the loudness grounded.
gen-gf-revalia-fs-erode: Revalia sprawls its widely spaced letters with a bold, expressive swagger. Erode, this text serif, settles in with shallow ascenders and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight.
gen-gf-revalia-fs-hoover: Revalia lets a bold, relaxed stride carry its widely separated letters across the line. Hoover, the classic serif, tightens things up with compressed ascenders and a generous entry into the e.
gen-gf-revalia-fs-trench-slab: Expressive from the first letter, Revalia spaces its letters widely and leaves the g open. Trench Slab, the serif underneath, brings dignity by keeping its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-domine: Bold Revalia strides wide across the heading line. Domine, the text serif, would carry paragraph after paragraph smoothly, its open curves and compact ascenders leaving the eye room.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-esteban: Loud, loose, hard to miss: Revalia strides wide while Esteban, a serif, keeps its lowercase oversized beside the capitals. The result is refined, with an e that never looks squeezed shut.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-faustina: A lowercase g with an open lower curve marks Revalia. Revalia is best at making loud, widely spaced letters, while Faustina, the text serif, handles bowls that thin gracefully and an open-jawed c.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-halant: Widely separated letters give Revalia a relaxed, unhurried stride. Halant, the classic serif, would read in a steady, traditional way, its faint thick-thin shift and towering x-height doing the work.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-headland-one: Revalia keeps its g's lower curve open and strides along with wide gaps between letters. Headland One, the classic serif, adds dignity with a gently varied stroke and a tall round o.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-hedvig-letters-serif: Revalia arrives loud, with widely separated letters and a g left open. Hedvig Letters Serif, the classic serif, steps in with sturdy, tall-bodied lowercase and medium contrast that gives the heading room to be loud.
